messages.author: d8d7a71c09861f31
messages.subject: Rstudio
parts:
Hello, I'm Isaac from Catalonia. I'm starting to use a Rstudio and I want to learn more. I want to know if is there is a book that allows me to get more knowledge about Rstudio in biostatistics analysis.

Can you or somebody recomended me some book?

Thank you

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: Rstudio
parts:
This may not be the appropriate list for R, but here goes.
Rstudio is an IDE that integrates text editing, R and many extra features into one package (environment). What you're looking for is "R books" or tutorials. Teh internets is crawling with freely accessable R resources. A whole book called series "useR!" is dedicated to certain fields and R. Also, other books often have snippets of R that help you push along a subject.
Bottom line, "google it" as old as it is, might be very appropriate here. If you have a genuine question about plotting data and/or how to use package ggplot2, feel free to drop another question.

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: 7fab6b1474f01cfb
messages.subject: Re: Rstudio
parts:
On Thu, 26 Mar 2015 23:35:06 +0100
Isaac Atienza <isaac....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello, I'm Isaac from Catalonia. I'm starting to use a Rstudio and I
> want to learn more. I want to know if is there is a book that allows
> me to get more knowledge about Rstudio in biostatistics analysis.
>
> Can you or somebody recomended me some book?
>
> Thank you
>

There is at least one book devoted to R Studio entitled "Getting
Started With R Studio" by John Verzani and published by O'Reilly. That
said, you probably want more information on R than R Studio. R Studio
is an IDE for R. It is not a GUI for R. You want to keep that in mind.

JWDougherty
